messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Alert: spike in container restarts on gpu-node-17 (srv-runtime). Multiple `CUDA ILLEGAL DEVICE ADDRESS` errors observed. Creating incident channel and paging oncall.
michael: seeing a cascade of container restarts from the serving pool, ~7 restarts in last 3m, p95 latency up. Logs show `cuda: illegal memory access` and process exits.
lara: grabbing crash log from one of the pods:
```
E tensorflow/serving: runtime error: CUDA illegal memory access
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
#0 0x7f8c1a3b bfd
#1 0x55aa4f2d runtime::serve::kv_cache
...
```
michael: stacktrace looks like a misaligned device pointer in the runtime allocator. Suspect a kernel-level race during page reclamation after eviction.
ops-oncall: I'm oncall, starting triage. Which customers impacted? any 5xx spikes tied to prod routes?
michael: two customers (cust-omega, cust-lucid) reported increased 500s ~10:23 UTC. Route /v1/generate shows errors. Temporary fallback already configured for some requests but not all.
eng-runtime-amy: probed the node, dmesg has this repeating:
```
[12345.678901] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=21456, pidName=serving
[12345.678905] BUG: could not handle page fault for address 0x7f7fffe1234
```
eng-runtime-amy: 79 Xid is illegal memory access. Might be a kernel driver or user-space quirk with our allocator after eviction.
lara: repro attempt on a staging replica triggered identical `misaligned pointer` log under heavy eviction/active batching.
ops-oncall: immediate mitigation proposals:
- cordon + drain gpu-node-17
- route traffic away from the affected serving pool
- restart pod(s) with `--disable-kv-cache` flag to avoid prefix cache path
ops-oncall: starting `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17` now.
infra-dan: I can push a temporary taint + scale up warm nodes to replace capacity. I'll add `gpu:hotpatch` taint and scale dedicated pool.
eng-runtime-amy: can we flip fallback to cpu-serving for affected users? that's slower but avoids GPU crash loop.
michael: enabling CPU fallback for cust-omega and cust-lucid now (feature flag: route-fallback=cpu). Notifying customers.
sre-bot: Deploy bot: rollout started: runtime-image@canary -> v5.12-hotfix (disable kv-cache). 6 pods updated so far.
ops-oncall: after cordon + drain, node shows zero active serving pods. New pods scheduled on other healthy nodes.
lara: logs from restarted pods show reduced crash rate; a handful of older pods still emitted one `misaligned pointer` during shutdown.
eng-runtime-amy: collecting `cuda-memcheck` trace and kernel oops; attaching a pointer dump snippet to incident doc. Proposed short-term: keep kv-cache disabled and add a retry/backoff on ILLEGAL access to trigger safe fallback.
infra-dan: scaled up warm nodes 3->6, traffic leveling holding.
michael: customer update: cust-omega acknowledged fallback, perf hit ~2x latency but no errors.
ops-oncall: monitoring for 15m before uncordon. If stable, we'll re-enable kv-cache on 1 pod to validate.
sre-bot: Metric alert cleared: serving-error-rate back to baseline on primary pool.
eng-runtime-amy: file an internal bug for possible kernel race in driver/allocator. Tagging `root-cause: kernel-pointer-race` and assigning to eng-ml.
lara: note for postmortem: reproduce requires heavy eviction + prefix cache active + long sequence lengths.
ops-oncall: plan: 1) full drain/patch cycle completed, 2) keep kv-cache off for 24h, 3) run longer memcheck/nightly repro, 4) customer follow-up and postmortem.
infra-dan: will open a maintenance window for planned reboot of gpu-node-17 tomorrow 03:00 UTC to pick up driver update.
michael: will draft customer impact note and set status_page to `degraded` for the two customers for the window we saw.
ops-oncall: marking incident as mitigated. Creating follow-up doc -> link: https://go/to/incidents/6155554321
sre-bot: Incident closed (mitigated). Follow-up owners: eng-runtime-amy, infra-dan. PM request for postmortem assigned to michael.
lara: thanks all, will attach repro logs and memcheck traces to the follow-up doc.
michael: closing thread here, will coordinate postmortem sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
